answer: Pairwise uniqueness challenges stop one operator from running many identities. Each epoch, a pairing vine links each identity to a random partner, and at a shared pulse both answer one fresh prompt in ten minutes. A pair passes only if both answers agree; each signal is checked against past answers, so copied scripts fail, and failure freezes both for one epoch. The k-th fake identity costs one more responder, about 30 credits, with no reuse across pairs; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 responders, about 30,000 credits per epoch, while an honest agent pays for one slot. Failure mode: stand-in rental.
